title: Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act
official_title: An Act to amend the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 relating to licensing transparency.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-34 on August 19, 2025. Sponsored by Rep. Ronny Jackson (R-TX) with two cosponsors; the export-control oversight measure passed both chambers before being signed.
summary: Requires the Secretary, under the Export Control Reform Act, to report to Congress every year on export-license decisions and end-use checks for exports to certain foreign entities — those located in Country Group D:5 countries and listed on Supplement No. 4 or No. 7 to part 744 of the Export Administration Regulations.
brief: Requires an annual report to Congress on export licenses and end-use checks involving covered entities in Country Group D:5 countries.

top_lines.headline: Annual Export-License Reporting
subs: The Secretary must report to Congress within one year, then at least annually
Covers license applications, authorizations, and end-use checks for covered entities
Each entry lists the applicant, item, end-user, location, value, and decision

top_lines.headline: Covered Entities Defined
subs: Applies to entities located in Country Group D:5 countries
And listed on Supplement No. 4 or No. 7 to part 744 of the Export Administration Regulations

top_lines.headline: Confidentiality
subs: Report details exempt from public disclosure except aggregate statistics
Information that could jeopardize an investigation must be excluded

items.main: Names the Act the “Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Amends Section 1756 of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to require an annual report on export-license activity involving covered entities.
items.detail: Within one year, and at least annually thereafter, the Secretary must report to the House Foreign Affairs Committee and Senate Banking Committee on end-use checks and on license applications and authorizations for the export, reexport, release, and in-country transfer of controlled items to covered entities. Each entry must give the applicant name, a description of the item (including the Export Control Classification Number), the end-user and location, a value estimate, the decision, and the submission date, plus aggregate statistics.

items.main: Defines covered entities and shields the report details from public disclosure.
items.detail: A covered entity is one located in a Country Group D:5 country under Supplement No. 1 to part 740 of the Export Administration Regulations that is also identified under Supplement No. 4 or No. 7 to part 744 of those regulations. The reported information, other than aggregate statistics, is exempt from public disclosure, and the Secretary must exclude anything that could jeopardize an ongoing investigation. The requirement is subject to the availability of appropriations.

underreported.summary: The annual reporting requirement is "subject to the availability of appropriations."
underreported.why_unreported: The caption is "Report," but the operative duty is made contingent on funding rather than unconditional.

underreported.summary: A covered entity must be both located in a Country Group D:5 country and listed on Supplement No. 4 or Supplement No. 7 to part 744 of the Export Administration Regulations.
underreported.why_unreported: Requiring both conditions narrows the report to a specific intersection of high-risk entities rather than all entities located in those countries.

gaps: The bill requires annual reporting but sets no penalty or consequence if BIS fails to submit the report.
The report covers covered entities in Country Group D:5 but does not address comparable-risk entities in other country groups.
The bill exempts the report from public disclosure except aggregate statistics but sets no schedule for releasing those statistics publicly.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Jackson
featured_quotes.text: today, we are bringing a very important piece of legislation to the floor, the Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act, a key piece of legislation to ensure our country stays ahead of our adversaries. Businesses and universities in the United States work constantly to innovate, improve, and invent the best technologies and systems in this world. This is what keeps America on the leading edge.

added: New annual BIS report to Congress on export licensing to covered entities (new 50 U.S.C. 4815(e))
modified: Amends Section 1756 of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to add the reporting requirement

added: New safeguard barring the required report from including any information that could jeopardize an ongoing investigation
modified: Annual report refocused toward end-use checks rather than enforcement actions generally
Reporting window shortened to the preceding one-year period
"Covered entity" narrowed to firms located in — not merely operating in — a Country Group D:5 country
Report element changed from "level of control" to "reason for control"
